hook.line: A stranger in the café keeps playing music out loud, and Tomás wants to ask without sounding rude. Spanish has a ceremonious way to ask for something.
hook.es: ¿Sería tan amable de bajar el volumen?
hook.en: Would you be so kind as to turn the volume down? (formal)

examples.es: ¿Sería tan amable de bajar el volumen?
examples.en: Would you be so kind as to turn the volume down? (formal)

examples.es: ¿Serías tan amable de ayudarme con esto?
examples.en: Would you be so kind as to help me with this? (informal)

examples.es: ¿Tendría la bondad de esperar un momento?
examples.en: Would you kindly wait a moment? (formal)

examples.es: ¿Sería mucho pedir que cerraras la puerta?
examples.en: Would it be too much to ask you to close the door? (informal)

examples.es: ¿Sería tan amable de repetir la dirección?
examples.en: Would you be so kind as to repeat the address? (formal)

examples.es: ¿Sería mucho pedir que, por una vez, llegaras puntual?
examples.en: Would it be too much to ask you to be on time for once? (informal)

rule:
For the most polite request, ask about kindness: *¿sería tan amable de…?* with a verb ending in *-r* (*de bajar*), or *¿tendría la bondad de…?*. With a friend it is *serías*, and it sounds ironic.

*¿Sería mucho pedir que…?* is different: it often carries a reproach. After *que* the verb is in the past subjunctive: *cerraras*, *llegaras*.

English says "would you be so kind". Spanish uses the same *would*: *sería*, *tendría*.
smallPrint: Teachers call these courtesy formulas. They use the conditional (*sería*, *tendría*), and *sería mucho pedir que* takes the imperfect subjunctive.

readAndPick.es: ¿Sería tan amable de bajar el volumen?
options: Would you (informal) be so kind as to turn the volume down?
Would you (formal) be so kind as to turn the volume down?
Would I be so kind as to turn the volume down?

readAndPick.es: ¿Serías tan amable de ayudarme con esto?
options: Would you (informal) be so kind as to help me with this?
Would you (formal) be so kind as to help me with this?

readAndPick.es: ¿Tendría la bondad de esperar un momento?
options: Did you kindly wait a moment?
Would you (formal) kindly wait a moment?
I will kindly wait a moment.

readAndPick.es: ¿Sería mucho pedir que cerraras la puerta?
options: Would it be too much to ask you to close the door?
Is the door closed?
Did you ask me to close the door?

readAndPick.es: ¿Sería mucho pedir que, por una vez, llegaras puntual?
options: Would it be too much to ask you to be late for once?
Would it be too much to ask you to be on time for once?
Would it be too much to ask you to be on time every time?
Will I sign here?
Did you kindly sign here?
Would you (formal) kindly sign here?
Would it be too much to ask me to help you?
Would it be too much to ask you to help me?

readAndPick.es: ¿Sería tan amable de moverse un poco?
options: Would you (formal) be so kind as to move a little?
Would you (informal) be so kind as to move a little?

yourTurn.prompt: Pick the right form and type the whole sentence, to a stranger: *¿___ tan amable de bajar el volumen?* (Sería or Serías)
yourTurn.answer: ¿Sería tan amable de bajar el volumen?
yourTurn.why: To a stranger you are formal, so *sería*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Would you (to a friend) be so kind as to help me with this?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Serías tan amable de ayudarme con esto?
yourTurn.why: To a friend it is *serías*; after *de* the verb ends in *-r*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Would you (formal) kindly wait a moment?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Tendría la bondad de esperar un momento?
yourTurn.why: *Tendría la bondad de* is the formal frame, then a verb ending in *-r*.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Would it be too much to ask you to close the door? (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: ¿Sería mucho pedir que cerraras la puerta?
yourTurn.why: After *sería mucho pedir que* the verb is in the past subjunctive: *cerraras*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it formal: *¿Serías tan amable de pasarme la sal?* Say: Would you (formal) be so kind as to pass me the salt?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Sería tan amable de pasarme la sal?
yourTurn.why: Drop the *-s*: *sería* is the formal version.

yourTurn.prompt: Turn the request into the ceremonious one: *Cierra la puerta.* Say: Would you (to a friend) be so kind as to close the door?
yourTurn.answer: ¿Serías tan amable de cerrar la puerta?
yourTurn.why: Put the verb after *de* in its *-r* form.

yourTurn.prompt: Type in Spanish: Would it be too much to ask you to be on time for once? (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: ¿Sería mucho pedir que, por una vez, llegaras puntual?
accept: ¿Sería mucho pedir que por una vez llegaras puntual?
yourTurn.why: *Llegaras* is the past subjunctive after *sería mucho pedir que*.

pitfalls.wrong: ¿Sería tan amable para bajar el volumen?
pitfalls.right: ¿Sería tan amable de bajar el volumen?
pitfalls.why: Almost. The frame is *tan amable de*, with *de*, not *para*.

pitfalls.wrong: ¿Sería mucho pedir que cierras la puerta?
pitfalls.right: ¿Sería mucho pedir que cerraras la puerta?
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *sería mucho pedir que* use the past subjunctive, *cerraras*.

pitfalls.right: ¿Tendría la bondad de esperar un momento?
pitfalls.why: Almost. *La bondad* needs *de* before the verb.

personal: Think of a small thing you could ask of a stranger, like closing a window, and ask for it in the most polite way you can with *¿sería tan amable de…?*.
